title: Prove the selected tensor phase needs exactly f+1 linear observations (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove that the absolute diagonal phase of selected MOVE24472's right monomial needs exactly **f+1 binary affine-linear observations** for every positive tensor column count f, even when observations mix columns arbitrarily. Claim type: scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration.

```text
r_j = XOR of coordinates {0,1,2,3,5,6} in column j
b   = XOR of coordinate 7 across all columns
Q_f = f + 3 sum_j r_j + 2b modulo 4
translation periods: every r_j = 0 and b = 0
```

The period subgroup has dimension 8f-1. A sufficient linear statistic must have its kernel inside that subgroup, giving the matching f+1 lower bound. The joint statistic saves f-1 observation bits against retaining the two natural parities separately in every column. This is an information bound, not a physical storage claim; nonlinear evaluation of Q_f itself has a two-bit output.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit CubeJerry #7426, head `172f4535ce8dcff79f626410af845f757c1563be`, for the recipe, source binding, literal implementation **and the existing one-column parity contraction**. Only the complete tensor period subgroup and sharp observation minimum are new. Retain aliromman #5375, #7000's native/Gaussian lineage and antunishdPursuit #6500's parity-expansion context. The general parity and quotient principles are classical. No predecessor executable was audited or replayed.

Only `research/selected-phase-linear-statistic/` is added. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8, selected #7000 unchanged. The formal-interface-lemma card explicitly changes scope to this written phase-information result. The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591467) predicted the f+1 bound; the [progress clarification](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19591585) credits the contraction already present in the predecessor's full proof.

## Evidence

- Before: the supplied recipe has a known contracted one-column phase, without a sharp all-column linear-observation minimum. After: an explicit joint statistic and a written all-f matching lower bound.
- `PASS_SELECTED_PHASE_LINEAR_STATISTIC`: every 512 one-column and 262,144 two-column address matches a separate literal strict-upper polynomial oracle. All 262,144 one-column derivative comparisons find 128 periods; constant derivatives classify every 262,144 two-column shift and find 32,768 periods. This uses independent column inputs, not 2^36 pairwise comparisons.
- Every one of 512 one-bit linear maps fails on its actual one-column fibers. A further 1,024 deterministic tensor fixtures at f=1..64, 3,072 Gaussian forward/inverse pairs, seven semantic negative controls, one positive cancellation control and five domain controls pass. Larger fixtures are not exhaustive.
- CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. Both registered warning-strict normal/optimized commands pass locally, timed at about 0.70 seconds each. Generated receipts bind all seven package files and agree between modes. Registered replay, AST/compile inspection and committed bytes/modes/source-history preflight pass. Official export integrity and both read-only Git-free exported replays pass, leaving all eight export files unchanged. No local registered check is deferred to CI.

From the repository root, another CPython 3.12 path may replace this interpreter:

```sh

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/selected-phase-linear-statistic/verify.py

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/selected-phase-linear-statistic --check-source-history --check-modes
```

The exported factual recipe is byte-identical to the cited predecessor file, SHA256 `96fadb44c3316be93c6c02f50cd2c841a9541d67b98fd94fc47b73fa64dd404c`. Its original source binding is a cited premise. The direct checker needs neither a pending Git object nor network access.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem concerns fixed affine-linear observations followed by arbitrary decoding of this exact absolute phase. It is not a general circuit minimum or a nonlinear streaming-space lower bound. Acquisition, decoding, dirty restoration, movement/layout, owner return, signed range, historical backing and the complete paid invoice remain unpriced. It supplies no physical tape/runtime reduction, supplier admission, new kappa or complete multiplication theorem. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected scientific cold replay, predecessor suite, Lean, Docker, independent human review or formal-kernel verification was run.

## Open next questions

- Implement the contraction in one supplied literal phase producer and charge every parity read, carry, cleanup and retained backing before quoting physical savings.
- Specify a reversible sequential scan computing the nonlinear two-bit phase without retaining all f linear observations. The present decoder is mathematical, with no priced streaming contract.

This contribution stops at the first new proved information bound and reserves no follow-up.

This proves a linear-information minimum for one selected tensor phase; neither result is a dependency of the other and no competing observation minimum is reported.

The own-open-PR completion check inspected the seven other contributions created since the CLAIM: #7501, #7502, #7504, #7505, #7506, #7507 and #7509. The related phase-bank result #7501 was already listed; #7509 replaces its earlier claim pointer above. The remaining scopes concern column-plane geometry, canonical rotation routing, exact inverse preparation, cubic repair and structured interaction errors. None reports a competing linear-observation minimum for this phase. No new mathematical computations were run to compare their results.

I read the checks once and the actual job log. It reports 760 tests, exactly one failure and 24 skipped. The failed test is `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`, at `tests/test_research_current_status.py:58`, with ``AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found`` in the CI verification document. I inspected the canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` Git objects. `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`; the current section of `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. The failing test requires the selected reproduction command in that section. These files and the test are unchanged by this PR, whose diff contains only the seven isolated package files.

I also read the actual failed-job logs for rohanarun's [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314), dillona's [run 42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790), and petalas runs [43437283229](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437283229) and [43437339750](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43437339750). Each has the same sole failed test, missing-command assertion, 760-test total and 24 skips. Run metadata confirms the first two fork owners as rohanarun and dillona. This establishes the shared repository-level blocker and supplies no mathematical coverage for this package.

All evidence in the Evidence section remains local at the unchanged head. Normal/optimized direct and registered checks, generated receipt equality, committed bytes/modes/source history, official export integrity and read-only Git-free exported replays passed. No fix, retrigger commit, push, job rerun or shared-file edit was made in response to this failure. Maintainers own the repair of main.
